# VORTEX COMPUTE

> Sovereign distributed GPU & NVMe-over-Fabrics inference engine for low-latency MoE models.

## Overview
VORTEX COMPUTE is a sovereign distributed inference engine that shards tensors across GPU nodes over RDMA fabric, verifies speculative token trees, pins hot page-cache to remote NVMe namespaces, keeps KV state in a zero-copy ring, applies deterministic quantization, and isolates every node in hardware enclaves. No external network dependency for inference.

## Architecture Pillars
- RDMA Tensor Sharding: tensors split across GPU nodes, transferred over RDMA without host-CPU staging.
- Speculative Tree Verification: draft model proposes token trees; target validates in one pass and accepts valid prefix.
- NVMe Page-Cache Pinning: hot pages pinned to remote NVMe namespaces, kept resident for repeated expert lookups.
- Zero-Copy KV Ring: shard metadata and KV state resident in pinned NVMe pages, resolved against the fabric.
- Deterministic Quantization: fixed bits-per-weight for reproducible, auditable outputs.
- Hardware Enclave Isolation: enclave-per-node isolation; assets, KV state, and telemetry stay inside the boundary.

## Deployment Tiers
- Edge Node 8GB (edge-8gb): 8 GB VRAM, 1,240 tok/s, 1.8 ms P99, batch 8, 1 enclave.
- Workstation 12GB (workstation-12gb): 12 GB VRAM, 3,480 tok/s, 0.9 ms P99, batch 24, 2 enclaves.
- Rack Pod 8xGPU (rack-pod-8xgpu): 64 GB VRAM, 18,600 tok/s, 0.42 ms P99, batch 64, 64 enclaves.

## Sizing Calculator Inputs
- Active parameters (B)
- Total MoE parameters (B)
- Bits per weight (bpw)
- PCIe generation (4/5/6)
- Batch size
